evidence.scope: Motivating tensor canonical conversion profile; no use of integrated apparatus.

research_question: Does direct rational scaling preserve tensor DFixed binary32 semantics while avoiding repeated wide division?
falsification_criterion: Any unexplained output mismatch blocks equivalence/performance claims; no lower operation count or no measured improvement on matched native corpus fails the applicable bounded improvement claim.
matched_control: Native existing-algorithm extraction and one direct rational alternative; same compiler, packed-trit arithmetic, representation, input order and checksum obligations.
method: Independent Fraction oracle from binary32 bits; extracted fixed/int arithmetic with governance removed; one direct numerator/denominator quotient for negative exponent, original multiply branch otherwise.
measurement_plan: One bounded corpus: both signs around all exponent boundaries, specials, fractions, quantization boundaries and 128 seeded finite random patterns. Correctness first. One warmup/candidate; six randomized paired full-corpus batches (three BC/CB), steady-clock integer ns; retain all attempts and mismatches. Stop on non-equivalence or approximate 60-minute active budget.
resource_requirements: No packages/network required for execution; approximately 60 minutes active cap
security_requirements: No VM/CLI/CanonFS/governance dependency or production edits
Read only source snapshots; write only research packet and temporary build outputs
